data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name Yaaqov meaning 'he supplants' or 'he deceives' (Jacob). In the Old Testament, Jacob was a deceiver and supplanter, who God blessed despite his imperfections. In the New Testament, St. James the Just, also known as Jacob, was a leader of the Jerusalem church. The name Jacobo carries the meaning “God's supplier” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Jacobo usually hope their child will grow to embody god's supplier and live with faith, good character and purpose.
